name: Fullscreen Moon and Mars exploration with controls
description: Surface dialogs fill the entire visible viewport and keep reachable controls without changing the outer-space flight.
steps: Open ?surface=moon and verify the surface fills the full browser viewport without a framed black margin
After astronaut exits, confirm the small right-aligned borderless W A S D pad and Moon Jump control
Return to orbit and open Mars, verifying its full-screen viewport and W A S D pad
Verify the original spaceship and NASA inspect dashboard still work
expected: Both landscapes use the full available viewport; smaller right-hand controls work and the original orbit remains accessible.

name: Moon astronaut emerges after touchdown and receives mission dialogue
description: A contextual pixel mission-control box narrates landing stages without blocking flight and gives the scan assignment only after crew exit.
steps: Observe APPROACH, DESCENT, and TOUCHDOWN communication messages while the astronaut is not yet outdoors
Wait until the hatch opens and see the astronaut walking from the ship to the field
After exit, verify the mission dialogue requests scanning all four artifacts, then try the E inspect command
expected: The astronaut exits after touchdown instead of teleporting; the mission briefing appears after the exit and scanning still works.

name: Mars astronaut emerges and receives scanning objective
covers: Mars instruments stay visible on descent
description: Mars shares the same mission dialogue lifecycle and crew-egress animation while preserving all equipment and proximity scans.
steps: Verify rover and lander images remain visible while the ship lands and the astronaut remains indoors
Watch the astronaut come out of the ship and walk toward the Martian field
Read the mission dialogue asking to scan all five machines
Approach Sojourner, press E, and scan it in the mission dashboard
expected: All Mars artifacts remain visible; the astronaut appears only after landing and the five-item scanning prompt is shown.

name: Responsive surface details and inspection boxes
description: Both terrains include more geological details, compact inspection UI, and an accessible mission briefing on mobile.
steps: Open Moon and Mars at a mobile viewport
Check both full-screen terrains have fine pixel landscape detail without blurring
Confirm contextual INSPECT card is smaller and near the selected object
Confirm the right-aligned WASD pad has no ornamental outlines and remains tappable
Dismiss the mission briefing using its close control, then keep walking
expected: The viewport remains filled; terrain details, inspection, dialogue and touch movement fit without overflowing.
